children: Consumers are feeling less pain at the gasoline pump these days, but pricing trends hint at a potential record-setting Thanksgiving Day, according to GasBuddy data.

Gasoline pump prices dipped below $4 a gallon this week for the first time since August, to an average of $3.95 a gallon on Tuesday afternoon, GasBuddy says. Oil prices overall have been falling, mainly on hopes for an end to the Iran war.
Gas prices are 18 cents below last week's average of $4.13 a gallon for regular unleaded, and 41 cents below the $4.36 per gallon average last month, according to GasBuddy data.
That's despite Tuesday's consumer price index showing that energy prices rose 0.7% in October from September, higher than the 0.4% increase for overall inflation.
Patrick De Haan, GasBuddy's head of petroleum analysis, expects average gasoline prices to keep falling, reaching about 75 cents to $1 a gallon below their Sept. 24 peaks by Thanksgiving.

But that doesn't mean a record is out of the question. The current Thanksgiving Day records are $3.56 for a gallon of regular unleaded and $5.25 a gallon for diesel. Both of those records were set in 2022, after Russia invaded Ukraine on Feb. 24 of that year.

The pre-election affordability push that prioritized making essentials like gasoline less expensive for struggling households doesn't have much to do with the current state of gas prices, De Haan says.

"Many will assume the election had something to do with it, but that's a myth," he said. "Gas prices have fallen in the 30 days leading up to the election every year since 2006 except 2010, and it's typically seasonal: refiners finish maintenance and ramp up output just as demand fades with cooler weather." After Sept. 13, gas stations can sell winter blend, which is cheaper to make than summer gas, and the biggest factor in falling prices, as gasoline demand cools off while supplies stay plentiful, he says.

Seasonal factors, along with more oil moving through the Strait of Hormuz, "are why prices could stay below $4 in the weeks ahead," De Haan wrote of gasoline pump prices. "That said, the election's outcome may send a message to Washington to sharpen its focus on affordability, and I'd expect even more attention on bringing prices down."
Diesel prices have also fallen, by about a dime a gallon from last week's average, to about $6.19 a gallon.
De Haan expects diesel prices, which have been falling about one to two cents a day, will still be below $6 a gallon this Thanksgiving.
GasBuddy, which compiles its data from more than 12 million price reports from over 150,000 gas stations, has seen more drivers reporting $2.99 a gallon prices, especially in the Great Lakes states.
Service stations in Ohio and Indiana could "definitely" be sub-$3 a gallon around Thanksgiving, "so DO NOT be in a rush to fill up!" De Haan posted on social media.

U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve supplies have dropped by 2.7 million barrels to 279.5 million, as the last 40 million barrels are now being released, and is also why prices have started falling noticeably dropping in recent weeks, he added.

The Energy Department announced on Sept. 29 that it was releasing 40 million barrels of crude from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, the last batch of a global deal to loan 172 million barrels from the emergency supply to about 30 countries to counter disruptions from the war in Iran.

Eleven states have seen average gas prices drop by 50 cents a gallon over the past four weeks, including North Carolina (down 76 cents a gallon); New Mexico (down 62 cents a gallon); Michigan (down 60 cents); California (down 60 cents); Idaho (down 57 cents); Alaska (down 54 cents); Utah (down 53 cents); Montana (down 52 cents); South Carolina (down 52 cents); Oklahoma (down 50 cents); and Arizona (down 50 cents). "Individual stations in these states may be down more than 75 c/gal," De Haan said.
